title: Saddle-Point Problems with a Low-Dimensional Block Do Not Need Accurate Inner Solves
summary: Many learning problems couple a high-dimensional block of parameters with a handful of adversarial or dual variables: worst-group risk over a few groups, or learning under a few constraints. We consider $\min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in Y} f(x,y)$ with $X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$, a compact convex set and strongly convex with condition number $κ$, and we count the oracle calls for $x$ and for $y$ separately. The textbook approach runs a cutting-plane method in $y$ and solves every inner problem to accuracy $\varepsilon$ with an accelerated method; it needs $O(m\log(1/\varepsilon))$ calls for $y$ but…
